title: Black-painted timber shiplap weatherboards on a dwelling (Rothesay Bay, Auckland)
jurisdiction: New Zealand (MBIE, Building Act 2004): comparative test only; not an Alberta case; no Alberta applicability asserted
code_edition: NZ Building Code B2/E2 as cited
document_type: MBIE determination under Building Act 2004 s188 (regulator decision on an individual matter); not an applicant's alternative-solution file

facts.text: Existing timber-frame dwelling with concrete block ground floor and vertical timber shiplap weatherboards at first floor, painted black; a new entranceway replaced a former conservatory.
Authority's proposed decision was to refuse a CCC because dark paint may cause the weatherboards to cup or split; matter is whether black-painted weatherboards comply with B2 as relates to E2.

Paint is a proprietary formula with a reported TSR of 23.8%; no TSR rating is available for the weatherboards; factors include orientation, shading, exposure, board size, drained and ventilated cavity, low thermal stress and maintenance documentation.
Absence of a manufacturer warranty does not by itself show non-compliance.
Draft determination accepted by the owner, the authority ('extremely reluctantly'), the LBP builder, the LBP supervisor and the registered architect.

limitations: Comparative only: a New Zealand determination used to test attachment format and content; it cannot establish Alberta performance or applicability.
